content: When pulmonary artery pressure (PAP), pulmonary-capillary wedge pressure (PCWP), pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR), and systemic vascular resistance (SVR) are elevated, reducing these parameters toward normal levels typically results in an increase in cardiac output. Conversely, intravenous nitroglycerin administration generally decreases cardiac output when given to patients whose central venous pressure (CVP), right atrial pressure (RAP), PAP, PCWP, PVR, and SVR are all within normal ranges. Most clinical trials involving intravenous nitroglycerin have been of short duration, often monitoring hemodynamic parameters during a single surgical procedure. In one meticulously conducted study, which extended beyond a few hours, continuous intravenous nitroglycerin lost nearly all of its hemodynamic effects after 48 hours. However, in the same study, patients who received nitroglycerin infusions for only 12 hours out of every 24-hour period did not exhibit a similar attenuation of effect. These findings align with results observed in multiple large, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials of other nitroglycerin formulations and nitrates. Nitroglycerin in 5% dextrose injection is supplied in large-volume glass containers. It should be stored at a temperature of 20 to 25°C (68 to 77°F) and protected from freezing. There is limited information available regarding patient counseling for nitroglycerin (injection solution in 5% dextrose) in the drug label. The interaction between alcohol and nitroglycerin (injection solution in 5% dextrose) has not been established. Patients are advised to consult their physician about the potential effects of consuming alcohol while using this medication. The brand name for this formulation is NITROGLYCERIN IN DEXTROSE®. There is limited information available regarding look-alike drug names for this product.
